flashcards.q: What wire format does MCP use, and what are the three message shapes?
flashcards.a: JSON-RPC 2.0. Request (has id, expects a response), response (id + result or error), notification (no id, no reply expected).

flashcards.q: Name the three MCP primitives and who decides to invoke each.
Which MCP spec revision does this module describe, and what is its headline change?
flashcards.a: 2026-07-28. It makes the protocol stateless: removes the initialize handshake and Mcp-Session-Id sessions.

flashcards.q: List the MCP spec revisions in order.
Why is HTTP+SSE deprecated as an MCP transport?
flashcards.a: It required sticky sessions (POST had to reach the instance holding the SSE stream), broke horizontal scaling, and had no clean resume after a dropped connection.

flashcards.q: A tool fails inside an MCP server. How should the failure be returned, and why?
flashcards.a: As a normal tools/call result with isError:true and content describing the failure, not a JSON-RPC error -- the model must see it as an observation to react to, not have the run killed by an exception.

flashcards.q: What is the confused-deputy problem as it applies to an MCP server?
flashcards.a: The server holds its own elevated credentials and acts on behalf of a caller (the model) that can be manipulated by injected content it reads, so it can be tricked into misusing its own authority.

flashcards.q: What is token passthrough and why does the MCP spec forbid it?
flashcards.a: Forwarding the client's bearer token straight to a downstream API. It breaks the audit trail, bypasses the server's own access policy, and leaks every forwarded user token if the server is compromised. Spec: MUST NOT.

flashcards.q: What replaces token passthrough as the correct pattern?
flashcards.a: Validate the incoming token's audience against the server's own identity, then use a separately held, narrowly scoped credential for the downstream call.

flashcards.q: What is sampling in MCP, and what happened to it in 2026-07-28?
flashcards.a: sampling/createMessage lets a server without model access ask the connected client to run a completion. Deprecated 2026-07-28; migration is to call a provider directly with your own key.

flashcards.q: How does elicitation work under the new stateless (2026-07-28) Multi Round-Trip Request pattern?
flashcards.a: The server returns an InputRequiredResult naming what it needs; the client retries the ORIGINAL request with inputResponses filled in, instead of the server pushing a new request mid-flight.

flashcards.q: Why are Roots being deprecated, and does that weaken sandboxing?
flashcards.a: Most implementations already pass paths as tool arguments or bake scope into config. Roots was always advisory (unenforced), so removing it doesn't remove any real control -- server-side authorization was always the actual boundary.

flashcards.q: What does resource indicators (RFC 8707) add to MCP auth, and when was it introduced?
flashcards.a: Introduced 2025-06-18. Scopes an issued OAuth token to one specific MCP server so it can't be replayed against a different server the client also holds a token for.

flashcards.q: When is MCP the wrong abstraction?
flashcards.a: One agent calling one in-process function -- MCP adds schema validation, serialization, and a subprocess spawn or network round trip to reach code that's already right there, with no portability benefit if nothing else will ever call it.

flashcards.q: State the one-paragraph distinction between MCP and A2A.
flashcards.a: MCP connects an agent to tools/context (client-to-server, resource-shaped). A2A connects agents to each other as peers (task-shaped, agent-card discovery, stateful task lifecycle). They compose, not compete.
